definitions.gloss: Tanabata decorations; ornamental strips and streamers for the Star Festival
definitions.explanation: Colorful paper decorations — primarily {短冊|たんざく} (paper strips with wishes), origami cranes, and streamers — hung on bamboo branches for the July 7 Tanabata festival.

examples.japanese: {七夕|たなばた}{飾|かざ}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{七夕|たなばた}{飾|かざ}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}んでいる→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
examples.english: Tanabata decorations are lined up along the shopping street.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧たち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{短冊|たんざく}→短冊：13674_tanzaku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{願|ねが}い{事|ごと}→願い事：14621_negaigoto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}いて→書く：00477_kaku⟧{七夕|たなばた}{飾|かざ}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{結|むす}んだ→結ぶ：02308_musubu⟧。
examples.english: The children wrote their wishes on paper strips and tied them to the Tanabata decorations.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{七夕|たなばた}→七夕：05633_tanabata⟧ (Star Festival, July 7) + ⟦{飾|かざ}り→飾り：02539_kazari⟧ (decoration). Refers collectively to the bamboo-and-paper decorations displayed in homes, schools, train stations, and shopping districts.

COMMON COMPONENTS:
- ⟦{短冊|たんざく}→短冊：13674_tanzaku⟧: paper strips inscribed with wishes
- ⟦{折|お}り{鶴|づる}→折り鶴：12782_orizuru⟧: origami cranes
- {吹|ふ}き{流|なが}し: streamers
- ⟦{笹|ささ}{飾|かざ}り→笹飾り：28858_sasakazari⟧: bamboo decoration (alternative name)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The Tanabata legend tells of two stars — Orihime and Hikoboshi — who can meet only once a year across the Milky Way. People write wishes on ⟦{短冊|たんざく}→短冊：13674_tanzaku⟧ hoping the stars will grant them. The Sendai Tanabata Festival is famous for its elaborate displays.
